item.description:
• Deckle is rewritten in Go on MyGo, which draws its window itself on the GPU. Typing in a long note takes about half the time it did, and Deckle now runs on macOS 13 or later, on Intel Macs too, and on Linux and Windows.
  • The first launch takes the settings, workspaces, tabs and places of the version before it, and from then on Deckle updates itself with smaller updates that download only what changed.
  • Settings are kept in a settings.json file rather than the user defaults.
  • Spell checking, the Edit menu's Spelling, Substitutions and Transformations submenus, and beta updates are gone for now.
  • A fresh look: the tree opens the folders of the note shown and marks it, the note list parts its notes with hairlines, an empty tab lists the shortcuts to begin with, the panels name their keys and quick open marks what matched, and the workspace switcher shows the workspace's name and folder.
  • Settings has a toolbar, a theme picker of swatches, previews of the editor's fonts and of Chinese and Japanese, and the version under Updates, and buttons, check boxes and sliders take the theme's accent color.
  • The find bar is one field, with the count of matches and the Match Case and Regular Expression toggles inside it, and ⇧↩ finds the previous match.
  • Search Notes lists a line once with every match in it marked, and its lines read without the tags of callouts and footnotes.
  • The tree builds only the rows in view: in a folder of thousands of notes, a frame, and so each keystroke, takes a fraction of a millisecond rather than tens of them. Opening a note scrolls the tree to it, and hairlines part the tabs not shown.
  • A long note no longer runs under the line at the bottom of the window.
  • Every item of a numbered list is a list item, not only the first.
  • A heading further down a note no longer names it: a note without one before its text is named after its file.
  • Clicking empty space in the tree, or Escape in the list, goes back to All Notes, and Deckle Help describes this version.
  • On Windows and Linux, the Help menu shows, with Check for Updates… in it.

• Each workspace opens in a window of its own, so several folders can be open at once in one app. File > New Window (⇧⌘N) picks another, the sidebar's switcher still replaces the window's workspace, and every window open at quit comes back at launch.
